questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a French candidature commits the applicant to sending
questions.learningObjective: identify the documents a French candidature comprises
questions.stem: An employer advertises a post and writes « Envoyez votre candidature avant le 15 mars ». What does the word carry in French hiring?

options.text: A CV and a cover letter, since candidature names the whole application rather than one document
Only the CV, since a cover letter is an optional courtesy that French employers may ignore
options.misconception: reads candidature as a single file and misses the cover letter the word implies

options.text: A written statement of availability, since an employer may not keep any other record of you
options.misconception: believes an employer is forbidden to keep written records of the people who apply

options.text: A reference from a former employer, whom the employer must write to before inviting you
options.misconception: assumes a reference is collected by the employer, when a candidate supplies it

questions.explanation: « Candidature » in French hiring names the whole application, and the two documents it normally takes are the CV and the lettre de motivation. The cover letter is not a courtesy that can be left out, because it is where the applicant says which post is being applied for and why that employer, and no other document carries either claim. The trap is reading the word as a synonym of a CV, on the model of an English-speaking system where the two documents have drifted apart.
questions.hint: Ask what the employer cannot learn from a CV alone.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What the top of a French CV leads with
questions.learningObjective: identify the opening block of a French CV and its limits
questions.stem: A recruiter reads several hundred French CV files. What belongs at the top of a French CV, and what is left out?

options.text: Name and contact details, then the position sought and the most recent work, with no photograph
A long personal statement, since the cover letter has not yet been read at that point
options.misconception: expects the argument to be repeated in the file before the letter is opened

options.text: A photograph and a date of birth, since a French employer is entitled to ask for both
options.misconception: believes personal details are required, when French practice bars age and marital status

options.text: Every course ever attended, so that no experience of the candidate is left out of the file
options.misconception: reads completeness as the goal, when a CV is read in seconds and length buries the post

questions.explanation: A French CV leads with identification and contact, then the title of the post applied for and the most recent experience, which is written in reverse date order. French guidance is firm that the file carries no photograph, no date of birth, no marital status and no number of children, because the law of 4 March 1978 protects private life and an employer who asked for those details would be asking for a reason to discriminate. The trap is the Anglophone file, where a photograph and an age are routine.
questions.hint: Ask which details a French employer is not entitled to ask you for.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The claim a French cover letter makes
questions.learningObjective: analyse the obligatory claim of a lettre de motivation
questions.stem: A cover letter begins « En réponse à votre annonce pour le poste de technicien de maintenance, je me permets de vous proposer ma candidature. » What claim is being made?

options.text: That the applicant applies for that named post, which is why the post and the advert are both named
That the applicant can start at once, which the present tense of the verb already guarantees
options.misconception: reads a tense of politeness as a statement of immediate availability

options.text: That the applicant holds the required diploma, which any letter written after an advert implies
options.misconception: believes the reference to an advert certifies a qualification the letter never mentions

options.text: That the applicant is already hired, since a candidature sent in writing binds the employer
options.misconception: confuses a declaration of intent with a contract, which needs acceptance as well

questions.explanation: A lettre de motivation must name the post and the employer, and the first paragraph exists to do exactly that: « en réponse à votre annonce pour le poste de… » ties the application to a published offer. A generic letter that could be sent to forty companies has failed the only test the format imposes, which is whether it shows the employer was read. The phrase « je vous propose ma candidature » is a proposal, not a hiring: nothing binds the employer until a contract is signed.
questions.hint: Ask whether the letter could be sent unchanged to a competing firm.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Why the opening interview question looks odd
questions.learningObjective: explain the intent of the open question asked first in a French interview
questions.stem: A French interview opens with « Parlez-moi de vous. » Why is that sentence unusual in writing?

options.text: It asks for a summary in the order the candidate chooses, not a biography in the order it happened
It invites a criticism of a previous employer, which a French interview is expected to provoke
options.misconception: expects candour about a former employer, and reads an open question as an attack

options.text: It requests a formal statement in the third person, as if the file itself were being composed
options.misconception: takes a spoken question to need the impersonal grammar of a written record

options.text: It conceals a question about salary, which an employer reaches only through general remarks
options.misconception: believes the topic is hidden inside a general opening, and so reads for a trap

questions.explanation: « Parlez-moi de vous » is an open question: the candidate chooses the order, selects what to leave out and decides how long to go on, which is why it is asked first and why the answer is judged on structure rather than on content. A good answer runs in chronological order, gives one or two concrete examples, and closes by turning back to the post on offer. The trap is expecting the question to contain the point; in a French interview the point is what the candidate decides to say.
questions.hint: Ask who decides what the question is about.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a formal French form of address signals
questions.learningObjective: infer the relationship signalled by vouvoiement with a title
questions.stem: An employee writes « Madame la directrice » and closes « Veuillez agréer, Madame, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées. » What has the choice of form signalled?

options.text: Distance combined with respect, since a title, a vouvoiement and a closing formula mark a hierarchy
Equality, since a formal address is what a French speaker uses between colleagues of equal rank
options.misconception: carries the English convention of a formal register over to a familiar workplace

options.text: Deference to age alone, which is the only thing a title records in a French letter
options.misconception: reduces a title to an age marker and ignores the rank the title actually names

options.text: Distance without respect, since vouvoiement signals coldness rather than courtesy in France
options.misconception: reads the polite formula as an insult, confusing warmth with professional courtesy

questions.explanation: French workplace register is carried by three things at once: the pronoun (vous rather than tu), the title (madame la directrice, monsieur le responsable), and the closing formula (« salutations distinguées » for a stranger or a superior, « salutations cordiales » for a colleague). Choosing all three at once marks a professional distance that is also respectful; choosing none of them would mark a familiarity a first week has not earned. The trap is importing the English sense that formality is coldness.
questions.hint: Ask what a closing formula chosen for a superior says that one chosen for a colleague does not.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a non-compete clause does
questions.learningObjective: explain the effect of a clause de non-concurrence
questions.stem: A contract of employment states a probationary period, a notice period, and a clause forbidding work for a competing firm for a set period after the contract ends. What does that clause do?

options.text: It limits where the employee may work for a set period after leaving, in exchange for compensation paid out
It fixes the hours the employee must keep, which is the one thing a schedule clause cannot do
options.misconception: reads a restriction on future employers as a statement about hours inside this one

options.text: It entitles the employee to the same post on better terms, which is what a seniority clause grants
options.misconception: turns a limitation on the employee into a benefit handed to the same employee

options.text: It cancels the notice period, since an employee under a restriction need not announce a departure
options.misconception: believes a clause about after departure can delete an obligation that applies before it

questions.explanation: A clause de non-concurrence forbids an employee from working for a competing business for a stated period after the contract ends, and French law makes it conditional: it is only valid if it is written, limited in time and in activity, and accompanied by a compensation paid by the employer. A clause that fails any of those conditions is void, so a candidate who is offered one is entitled to ask what the compensation is. The trap is treating a restriction on future work as a benefit, when it is a price paid for the job.
questions.hint: Ask what the employee receives in exchange for giving up the right to work elsewhere.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Gross pay and take-home pay
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a gross figure from the sum actually paid
questions.stem: An offer states « salaire brut annuel de 2 400 euros ». A reader concludes the employee will receive 2 400 euros a month. What corrects it?

options.text: The figure is gross, and income tax and the employee's social contributions are deducted before payment
The figure is a monthly one, so a yearly total is reached only after those deductions are made
options.misconception: reads an annual gross figure as a monthly net one and doubles the mistake in one step

options.text: The figure is the ceiling of a range, and the exact amount is settled after the probation period
options.misconception: takes a stated offer as a provisional range rather than as a fixed contractual figure

options.text: The figure already contains the employer's charges, which are added to what the employee receives
options.misconception: confuses the employer's part of the contributions with money that reaches the employee

questions.explanation: A « salaire brut » is the figure before deduction. The employee sees a « net à payer », from which the employee part of the social contributions and the income tax are withheld. Employer contributions are calculated on the gross figure and never reach the employee, which is why a gross figure cannot be converted into a take-home one by simple subtraction and why a candidate is advised to ask about the net. The trap is reading a contract figure as a receipt.
questions.hint: Ask which of the two figures would be printed on a payslip.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: How a French working day is written
questions.learningObjective: parse a schedule written with paired time ranges
questions.stem: A post reads « du lundi au vendredi, de 8 h à 12 h et de 13 h 30 à 17 h 30 ». How is the working day expressed?

options.text: Two blocks of hours separated by the midday break, each written as a start and an end time
One continuous block, since the gap in the middle is a pause that the hours do not mention
options.misconception: assumes a single continuous block and loses the break that the two ranges announce

options.text: A duration written in hours, with the same start and end time kept on every working day
options.misconception: looks for a single number and reads the paired times as decoration

options.text: A weekly total, since the two blocks are added together and reported as one figure
options.misconception: adds the blocks and mistakes the result for a figure the employer actually wrote

questions.explanation: The pattern « de X à Y et de Z à T » is how a day with a break is written, and the two ranges tell the reader both the hours and the pause. This is the schedule of a « journée continue », a day organised in two parts rather than a single block with a long gap in the middle. The trap is reading the second range as extra availability rather than as the second half of one day, which would silently add an hour to every day of the week.
questions.hint: Ask how many separate blocks of work the sentence promises.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a rotating shift post involves
questions.learningObjective: interpret the vocabulary of rotating shifts
questions.stem: A hospital post is advertised as « horaires postés, roulement 3x8, week-end de repos ». What does the post involve?

options.text: Successive eight-hour shifts through the morning, the afternoon and the night, on a rotation
A fixed morning from Monday to Friday, with a weekend rota agreed from one month to the next
options.misconception: reads shift work as a fixed morning and misses that the point is the rotation

options.text: Twelve hours of work spread across the year, with the dates chosen by the employee
options.misconception: confuses a shared rota with a block of hours the employee allocates for themselves

options.text: One night shift each week, with the remaining days of the week left to the employee
options.misconception: takes one night a week as the whole arrangement rather than as one turn in a rota

questions.explanation: « Horaires postés » means work organised in shifts rather than in fixed office hours, « roulement 3x8 » is the rotation through three eight-hour shifts a day, and « week-end de repos » states that the weekend is not part of the rota. The three pieces together describe a cycle: the employee moves between posts through the day and night, and rests at the weekend. The trap is reading only « week-end de repos » as a promise of ordinary hours, when it says nothing about the other five days.
questions.hint: Ask what the figure eight is counting in « 3x8 ».

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The right to stop work in a dangerous situation
questions.learningObjective: explain the droit de retrait in French workplace safety
questions.stem: A French workplace rule requires safety shoes on a site and adds that an employee facing a grave and imminent danger may stop work. What is the second provision?

options.text: A right to withdraw, which lets the employee leave the danger without being treated as a refuser
An obligation to warn, which requires the employee to report the danger before leaving the place
options.misconception: turns a permission to withdraw into a duty to report first, which is a different right

options.text: A duty to continue, which requires the employee to finish the task and report it afterwards
options.misconception: inverts a safety right into an instruction to work through a danger that is in view

options.text: A right to resign, which lets the employee leave the job rather than the dangerous situation
options.misconception: reaches for the strongest sanction available, where the rule only suspends the obligation to work

questions.explanation: Le droit de retrait lets an employee stop work when a situation presents a grave and imminent danger, and the protection that goes with it means an employer may not treat the stopping as a refusal. The provision is about the situation, not the job: the employee leaves the danger, not the post, and an alert is still required where the danger is not yet grave. The trap is reaching for « démission », which ends the contract, when the rule only suspends the duty to work.
questions.hint: Ask whether the provision ends the contract or suspends an obligation.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a union negotiates and who it covers
questions.learningObjective: explain the reach of a convention collective
questions.stem: A pay-rise letter cites « la convention collective » and the site is described as having a union presence. What does the agreement do?

options.text: It fixes pay, hours and conditions for a whole trade, and it binds every employer inside that trade
It writes the contract of each employee, so a rise of any kind needs a fresh contract
options.misconception: treats a trade-wide agreement as a private contract between one employer and one person

options.text: It appoints the manager of the site, since the staff side chooses who runs the workplace
options.misconception: believes a union appoints management, whereas management is appointed by the employer

options.text: It settles disputes as a court would, which is why its decision closes the matter for good
options.misconception: confuses a negotiated text with a court ruling, so expects the matter to be closed for ever

questions.explanation: A « convention collective » is negotiated between the trade unions and the employers' organisations of one trade, and it sets the minimum pay, hours and conditions for every employee in that trade, whether or not they belong to the union. That collective effect is the point: an individual agreement cannot offer less. The trap is reading it as a list of individual contracts, which is why a pay letter can quote it while the contract itself stays untouched.
questions.hint: Ask who else in the same trade is bound by a text quoted in one company's letter.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The ordinary route of a disagreement about a dismissal
questions.learningObjective: sequence the stages of a French labour dispute
questions.stem: An employee believes a dismissal was unfair. Which order of steps is the ordinary route through the French system?

options.text: A written request, a meeting held for conciliation, then a claim before the labour court if nothing is agreed
A complaint to the police, a trial, and only afterwards any attempt to talk to the employer
options.misconception: assumes criminal procedure settles a dismissal, when dismissal is a civil matter between parties

options.text: A meeting with a union, a ruling by that union, and a payment fixed on the strength of the ruling
options.misconception: treats a union as a tribunal, though it negotiates and cannot award compensation

options.text: A complaint to a ministry, a national vote among the staff, and then a fresh election of the manager
options.misconception: expects the state to choose the outcome by a vote, which is not how a contract dispute is settled

questions.explanation: The route runs from a written claim to the employer, to a conciliation meeting that the employer must convene within a short statutory period, and then to the « prud'hommes », the labour court made up of lay and elected judges. The conciliation step is not a formality to be skipped but the point at which many files are settled, which is why a letter often states that the employee has asked for it. The trap is reaching for criminal law, which handles violence and fraud, not a contract.
questions.hint: Ask which kind of court a dismissal dispute is brought before.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Adjusting a post to a health condition
questions.learningObjective: identify an aménagement de poste and its limits
questions.stem: After a health problem an employee keeps the same job, but the workstation and the hours are changed on the advice of the occupational physician. What is that?

options.text: An adjustment of the post, which changes the workstation, the equipment or the working time of the job
A promotion, which raises the employee's grade and pay in recognition of the change made
options.misconception: confuses an adaptation of the job with a rise in grade and pay

options.text: A redeployment, which transfers the employee to another employer within the same group
options.misconception: reads accommodation as a move to a different employer, which is redeployment

options.text: An extension of the contract, which lengthens the probationary period until the post is usable
options.misconception: treats the arrangement as a delay in hiring rather than as a change to an existing job

questions.explanation: An « aménagement de poste » adapts the conditions of a job a person already holds: different equipment, a different workstation, a change of hours, sometimes part-time working. The opinion comes from the médecin du travail, and the employer keeps the contract and the pay. The distinction that matters is between adapting the post and moving the worker; a redeployment sends the person to another employer, whereas an aménagement keeps them where they are.
questions.hint: Ask whether the contract of employment is still the same one.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The usual basis of a promotion
questions.learningObjective: name the criteria weighed when a promotion is justified
questions.stem: An employer must justify a promotion to a trade union that has asked about it. Which basis is normally given?

options.text: Results against stated objectives, the skills shown and seniority, weighed together rather than separately
The opinion of the direct manager alone, since nobody else is placed to judge the work well
options.misconception: assumes a supervisor's opinion settles a question that is asked in writing

options.text: Length of service alone, because French practice ranks employees by time rather than by results
options.misconception: believes seniority alone decides, which is the one criterion a defence rarely accepts

options.text: The absence of any complaint, which is treated as proof that the work has been done properly
options.misconception: treats silence as evidence, where the file is expected to contain a positive account

questions.explanation: A promotion is normally argued from three sources at once: objectives set beforehand and met, skills acquired and proved, and « ancienneté », which is length of service and counts as a tie-breaker rather than as a title of its own. The reason all three are named is that a decision argued on one of them alone is easy to contest, and an employer asked to justify it has to be able to point to more than a preference. The trap is presenting seniority as sufficient, which is the argument most often rejected.
questions.hint: Ask which of the three is a tie-breaker rather than a claim in itself.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a performance review has to produce
questions.learningObjective: identify the output that makes a review usable
questions.stem: A French employer holds an annual review with each employee and wants the meeting to be worth the hour it takes. What has the review to produce?

options.text: Written objectives for the year ahead, since a review with no objectives has nothing to measure against
A note on the employee's private life, so that the personnel file is complete on every point
options.misconception: expects the employer to gather personal details that French practice excludes from the file

options.text: A decision on salary taken in the room, since the review is the only moment pay can move
options.misconception: believes the meeting is the only chance to discuss pay, overlooking the separate negotiations

options.text: A ranking of every employee from best to worst, published so that the standard is visible
options.misconception: assumes a ranking is published, where the review is confidential between the two parties

questions.explanation: The point of « l'entretien professionnel » is to close the past period and open the next one, and the only part that does real work is the set of objectives agreed in writing at the end. Results of the professional assessment must also be notified in writing, so that the employee can contest them. Without written objectives the following year has no baseline, which is why a review that only praises or only warns is regarded as a wasted hour.
questions.hint: Ask what the employer will be held to twelve months later.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The procedure that protects an employee facing dismissal
questions.learningObjective: sequence the procedural protections before a dismissal for misconduct
questions.stem: A French employer dismisses an employee for serious misconduct. What has the employer had to do before the dismissal took effect?

options.text: Convene the employee to one or more interviews beforehand, let them prepare, then notify the decision
Obtain an order from the labour court, since no dismissal is ever valid without prior approval
options.misconception: believes a judge authorises each dismissal, when the court's role comes after the decision

options.text: Pay the whole salary in advance, since the employer must fund the payment before giving notice
options.misconception: thinks payment in advance is required, when money paid at the end is the normal settlement

options.text: Ask the employee to resign, since a dismissal is valid only if the person agreed to leave
options.misconception: assumes consent is needed, when a dismissal is precisely a decision taken without it

questions.explanation: A dismissal for misconduct is only valid if « la procédure de licenciement » was followed: the employee is summoned by a letter with reasons, may prepare and be assisted, is heard in one or more interviews, and only then receives the notification. The delay between the summons and the interview and between the interview and the notification are both fixed, and a breach makes the dismissal void rather than merely unfair. The trap is expecting the employee to consent, which is the opposite of what dismissal is.
questions.hint: Ask what the employer must have in the file to show afterwards.

questions.topic: What makes a resignation valid in France
questions.learningObjective: identify the form and the cost of a démission
questions.stem: An employee decides to leave a French job of their own accord. What makes the resignation both valid and expensive?

options.text: Notice must reach the employer in writing, and the notice period in the contract has to be observed
One word spoken to the manager is enough, and it ends the contract from that day onwards
options.misconception: believes an oral word ends the contract, which leaves the employee without proof of the date

options.text: A registered letter to the tax office is needed, since only the state may end a contract
options.misconception: sends notice to the wrong body, since the employer is the party to the contract

options.text: A request to a union is needed, and the union then fixes the length of the notice period
options.misconception: assumes a third party sets the date, whereas the notice period comes from the contract

questions.explanation: A « démission » is valid when the employee makes it clear to the employer, in practice by a letter, and observes the notice period set by the contract or the collective agreement; the balance of the salary and of any leave is then paid at the end. The period is counted in months and the employee cannot simply shorten it because a better offer has arrived. The trap is treating the notice as a courtesy, when it is an obligation the employee owes.
questions.hint: Ask which party has to be told, and how many months afterwards the salary stops.

questions.topic: What a telework agreement settles
questions.learningObjective: describe the content and effect of a French telework agreement
questions.stem: A French employer signs an agreement that states it does not modify anyone's contract and applies to all staff. What is the agreement for?

To turn the employee's home into a workplace, so the employer's liability rules stop applying

questions.topic: The first move in a workplace conflict
questions.learningObjective: identify the first procedural step in handling a team conflict
questions.stem: Two colleagues on one team can no longer work together and their manager has not separated them. What does a French employer normally do first?

options.text: Hear each person separately, then establish the facts, since a conflict is a file before it is a feeling
Move the colleague with the shorter record, since length of service settles such matters by rule
options.misconception: applies a tie-break rule that has no standing in a dispute between two colleagues

options.text: Send both of them to the personnel office together, so that the two accounts can be compared

questions.topic: What a compte rendu is for
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a meeting record from a formal minute
questions.stem: A French team meeting is announced with « ordre du jour » and closed with a « compte rendu » sent afterwards. What is the second document for?

options.text: Recording what was decided and who will act, so the team shares one version after the meeting
Serving as a signed minute usable in court, which is why it is different from a formal minute
options.misconception: conflates an internal record with a « procès-verbal », which is the signed legal form

options.text: Listing the points in advance, printed beforehand so that everyone arrives having prepared
options.misconception: moves the document to the wrong moment, treating the list of points as the record

options.text: Informing absent members only, so that those present have no need to read it again
options.misconception: pictures a note sent only to the absent, when it goes to the whole team

A « procès-verbal » is the formal, signed instrument that can serve as evidence, and the two words are not interchangeable in French administrative practice. The « ordre du jour » is the list of points and belongs before the meeting, which is the confusion behind the third option. The purpose of the record is to stop the same discussion restarting the following week.

questions.topic: What a slippage in a schedule declares
questions.learningObjective: interpret the vocabulary used to announce a delay
questions.stem: A delivery that was due on 30 April is now expected on 15 May, and the report calls it « un glissement de deux semaines ». What does the phrase tell a reader?

questions.topic: A method for reading a French contract before signing
questions.learningObjective: describe a method for extracting obligations from a French contract

answer.exemplar: Four questions, and none of them is a question about tone. First, what is the base: the clause fixes a weekly figure and the question asks what counts as an hour beyond it, because a contract that says overtime is payable does not say which hours are not part of the week. Second, what is the rate: the clause gives a percentage, and the question asks whether the rate rises with the number of hours or stays flat, since a flat rate rewards a long week rather than a short one. Third, what the cap is, because a cap of a certain number of hours is what decides whether the rate is ever reached. Fourth, what the collective agreement adds, since a clause below the minimum in the applicable convention is not the whole rule. Apply it to « quatre heures supplémentaires par semaine au taux prévu par la convention collective »: the base is the contractual week, the rate is whatever the convention fixes rather than whatever the contract says, the cap is four hours, and anything above the cap is a separate question that the contract has not answered. Three of the four questions have answers in the document; the fourth sends the reader outside it, which is the correct result and not a failure.

questions.explanation: The method works because all four questions are asked of the text rather than of the intention behind it, and because each has a written answer or an explicit absence. Contracts are long, and the clause that causes a dispute is rarely the one a reader remembers from the interview. What to watch is the habit of reading for reassurance, looking for the sentence that sounds fair and stopping there, since the sentence that will be quoted in a dispute is the one about the cap or the rate.

First, ask what the figure is: a number without a label is not a salary but a guess, and the check is to establish whether it is a « brut annuel », a « net à payer », a monthly amount or an annual amount including a bonus that is not guaranteed. Second, ask what it contains, because a stated figure may or may not include a bonus, a car allowance or overtime, and those three items are worth more than the base suggests and less than the total implies. Third, ask what it is measured against, which means the applicable collective agreement: the grids of the convention fix a minimum for the classification, and an offer below the minimum is not a low offer but an unlawful one. Applied to an advert reading « salaire brut annuel de 2 400 euros, primes calculées chaque mois »: the label establishes the base, the second half of the sentence establishes that a variable element exists without stating it, and the grid establishes the floor. The candidate who cannot answer the third question is not ready to compare two offers, because the comparison is between classifications and not between sums.

questions.explanation: The order matters, because each check narrows what the next one can be applied to: a gross figure cannot be compared with a net one, and a classified post cannot be compared with an unclassified one. The method costs no arithmetic at all, which is why it is teachable, and its hardest step is the third, since it requires the learner to go and find a document outside the advertisement. What to watch is the habit of converting percentages in one's head, which produces a number nobody can check.

The method is deliberately text-based, so that it can be applied to a printed notice in a corridor as well as to a contract. Then state what each payment buys, since a rent buys use and a loan buys an asset, and the balance at the end of the loan is the difference between them. Applied to the figures: 900 a month is more than 650, and neither figure is the answer, because the ninety euros a month are buying a share of a building that the rent will never return. questions.explanation: The method works because it forces the two options onto the same horizon before it compares anything, and because the horizon is where almost all real errors in housing comparison are made. Its weak point is the assumption that increases can be projected, which the method handles by naming the assumption rather than by hiding it in a number. What to watch is the temptation to stop at the monthly figure, which is the only comparison that requires no work at all.
questions.hint: Ask what has to be done to the two figures before they can be compared at all.

answer.exemplar: Four readings, in this order. Read the decision first, in the first lines, and classify it as a grant, a partial grant or a refusal, because a letter may state two of these and the weaker one is what will be enforced. Read the facts next, and mark any that the applicant believes to be wrong, since a challenge must identify what is contested and not merely express dissatisfaction. Read the legal basis, which is named in the letter and which points to the text to be looked up, because the whole challenge is built on that text. Read the remedies last, and note both the time limit and the two possible routes, an appeal to the same body and an appeal to the administrative court. Applied to a refused benefit: the refusal is the decision, the income figure is the fact to contest if it is wrong, the text cited is the basis, and the letter's own statement of the routes is the answer to the question of what to do next. A reader who stops at the first paragraph has the news and no remedy.

questions.explanation: The order is the method, because each reading gives the next one its subject: the decision tells the reader which facts matter, the facts tell the reader which text to look up, and the text tells the reader whether the appeal is worth making. It also works for a favourable letter, since the remedies section then states the conditions the grant is subject to. What to watch is reading for the tone, which in administrative French is deliberately neutral and carries no information about the chances of an appeal.

answer.exemplar: Stage one: the higher salary hides a relocation cost that is not a single sum, because it includes the move itself, the deposit and the first months of an unfurnished flat, the difference between two housing markets, the travel back to see people already there, and the time it takes to become useful in a new team, which in a first year is not a salary at all. The lower salary hides the cost of the place: a commute, a shared kitchen, a town where the professional contacts are elsewhere, and a ceiling, since a post in a small market tends to follow the person rather than the salary. The trap is that both costs are real and neither appears in a figure. Stage two: I would check the higher salary with a third party and the lower one with nobody, because a salary figure is checkable and a life is not. The check would be with someone who has worked in that city for at least two years, and the question would not be about the money at all: I would ask what a working week actually looks like, who decides the hours, and whether the advertised figure is gross or net. The net figure is the one that pays the rent. The lower offer I would check by reading the contract twice, since the things it omits are the things I would be signing.

questions.explanation: The stages are separated because a relocation cost is a calculation and a professional ceiling is not, and treating the second as a calculation is the usual way a good salary turns out to be a bad year. Checking the salary with a third party is cheap and the check is decisive; checking the place with a third party produces opinions rather than information, which is why it is not done. What to watch is the habit of comparing two offers on one axis, when the whole point is that they are not on the same axis.
questions.hint: Ask which of the two costs can be reduced by asking one more question before signing.
